hero.name: Anmol Prabhakar
hero.focus: Focus: Electromechanical Integration, Mechanism Kinematics, and Wearable Biosensors

paragraphs: I build mechanical systems at the boundary where hardware interacts directly with the physical world and the human body. My focus is bridging my engineering skills with a biological frame of thinking to solve human problems. Through hands-on prototyping and electromechanical integration, I have been building functional robotic projects and experimenting with physiological technologies, such as EMG and EEG biosignals, as intuitive control systems.

flagshipProjects.title: 7-DOF Tendon-Driven Bionic Hand
flagshipProjects.subtitle: Robotic Hand with Kinematic Posture Control
flagshipProjects.description: A custom 3D-printed robotic hand designed to replicate natural finger motions and grip postures in real time. Built with snap-fit pin joints and internal channels for routed Dyneema tendons, it is driven by micro servos and a TI MSP432 microcontroller to execute smooth pinches, fists, and gestures.

flagshipProjects.title: Unified Smart Lighting Hub
flagshipProjects.subtitle: ESP32, BLE & 433 MHz RF Remote Integration
flagshipProjects.description: A centralized smart controller that connects multiple incompatible room and desk lights into one unified web dashboard. Built on an ESP32 web server, it bridges reverse-engineered Bluetooth signals and cloned 433 MHz RF remote frequencies with Cloudflare integration for control from anywhere.

aboutBio.degree: B.S. in Bioengineering | Minor in Electrical Engineering
paragraphs: I am a Bioengineering student with an Electrical Engineering minor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, focusing on designing physical hardware that interfaces directly with human movement and physiology. My technical interests span biomechatronics, wearable neural and muscular control interfaces (EEG and EMG), custom prosthetics and orthotics, and rapid electromechanical prototyping.

On campus, I work on hardware development with the Attune Neurofeedback EEG team, where I design modular headset mechanics and low-noise sensor housings. I also lead technical workshops for the Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES), teaching fellow students parametric CAD modeling, tolerance design, and 3D printing for functional hardware.
coursework: BIOE 210: Linear Algebra for Biomedical Data
CS 101: Intro Computing for Engineering & Science

bullets: Designed modular EEG headset enclosures in Onshape with snap-fit retention, allowing electrode cartridges to be swapped quickly without tools while staying secure during head movement.
Engineered internal wire routing channels across multiple CAD iterations to eliminate sharp bends, prevent wire wear, and shrink the overall housing footprint.
Developed an adjustable compliant headband mechanism that maintains comfortable, even contact pressure across different head sizes to reduce motion artifacts.
Collaborated with the electrical team to refine sensor interconnects and shield low-voltage neural signals from ambient electrical interference.
Fabricated custom carbon-fiber and thermoplastic orthotic shoe inserts using vacuum forming and heated press lamination tailored to individual patient biomechanics.
Shaped and finished composite orthotic shells on rotary grinding machinery to fit smoothly inside patient footwear while preserving structural arch support.
Scanned patient foot morphology with optical 3D surface scanners and mapped pressure points to build targeted cushioning zones for diabetic care.
Communicated directly with Spanish-speaking patients during clinical visits and fittings to verify symptom relief and fine-tune final insert comfort.
Assembled custom adult and pediatric Knee-Ankle-Foot Orthoses (KAFOs) and lower-limb braces, aligning structural aluminum uprights with the patient's natural joint axes.
Calibrated mechanical drop-lock knee hinges to provide stable support while standing and smooth unlocking when sitting.
Created positive plaster limb casts from patient measurements to vacuum-form rigid polycarbonate brace shells contoured to complex anatomy.
Observed patient walking trials to identify pressure spots and adjust brace alignment for a more natural, balanced gait.
Led the mechanical design and full CAD modeling of 6 competition robots in Onshape within strict tournament size constraints.
Prototyped and built high-speed game element intakes, multi-stage linear lift slides, and custom belted mecanum drivetrains for agile field navigation.
Manufactured custom robot parts in-house using 3D printers and manual shop tools alongside waterjet-cut aluminum structural plates.
Guided a 7-member team through design and build cycles across 6 seasons, earning multiple engineering design awards and advancing to the Regional Championship Finals.
